top_signals.title: What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening
top_signals.summary:
Four years into Russia’s war against Ukraine, what should the U.S. military have learned by now? Michael Kofman (Carnegie Endowment), Dara Massicot (Carnegie Endowment), and Amos Fox (Arizona State University) join Ryan to discuss. The easy answer is drones and AI, but our guests argue the harder truths lie elsewhere: “Old-fashioned” ideas like campaigning, holding territory, mass, and attrition still decide wars. And, as they discuss, based on U.S. performance in the war with Iran, it may be that not much learning has happened at all.Image: ArmyInform

top_signals.title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
top_signals.summary:
Purpose

CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938. This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK). Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution.

Actions to take

CISA urges organizations to take the following actions:

  • Identify affected Java installations. Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances. Note: JDKs and Java runtimes may not appear as separate entries in software inventories.
  • Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available, prioritizing internet-facing systems.
    • If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access.
  • Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions.
  •  Monitor for indicators of suspicious activity, including rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes.

Resources

CISA urges network defenders to review the following resource and apply necessary updates:

Vendor Guidance

  • Oracle’s Security Advisory: Critical Security Patch Update – November 2026

top_signals.title: Dangote Refinery Set to Start Trading in Lagos on Dec. 1
top_signals.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE will rank as the biggest company with a primary listing in Africa once it makes its trading debut in Lagos. The operation owned by tycoon Aliko Dangote is valued at the equivalent of about $48 billion through its initial public offering. Bloomberg's Jennifer Zabasajja reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026
top_signals.summary: Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)–personal income less personal current taxes–increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent). Personal outlays–the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments–increased $113.0 billion in September. Personal saving was $911.1 billion, and the personal saving rate–personal saving as a percentage of DPI–was 3.8 percent.

top_signals.title: U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026
top_signals.summary: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit decreased in September 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit decreased from $105.7 billion in August (revised) to $105.0 billion in September, as exports increased more than imports. The goods deficit decreased $0.7 billion in September to $135.9 billion. The services surplus decreased less than $0.1 billion in September to $30.9 billion.

alerts.title: GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026
alerts.summary: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.
